ns0:entry.ns0:content:
fix(streaming): give the trainer's data-parallel rank to the streaming dataset (#4890)

The streaming dataset reshards in the DataLoader worker from RANK and WORLD_SIZE,
because torch.distributed is not initialized there. A launcher that does not export
RANK made every rank stream the full dataset. make_dataloaders now passes dp_rank
and dp_world_size, which take priority. Direct use is unchanged.

ns0:entry.ns0:title: fix(configs): backfill pretrained_path in PreTrainedConfig.from_pretr…
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
fix(configs): backfill pretrained_path in PreTrainedConfig.from_pretrained (#4648)

* fix(configs): backfill pretrained_path in PreTrainedConfig.from_pretrained

config.json only carries train-time fields, so parsing it yields a config
with pretrained_path=None. When such a config is passed to make_policy() /
make_pre_post_processors() (the documented programmatic path), the factory
silently takes the 'from scratch' branch and builds a processor pipeline
with empty normalization stats instead of loading the pretrained safetensors.
The policy loads without error but acts blind (raw pixel/state values go
in, near-random actions come out); on PushT with lerobot/diffusion_pusht
this silently degrades a 118-reward policy to ~5.

Backfill pretrained_path / pretrained_revision on the config returned by
from_pretrained(), matching what the CLI parser does for --policy.path.

Verified on the migrated lerobot/diffusion_pusht checkpoint: identical
manual rollout code scores cum=4.8 / max=0.016 without the backfill and
cum=199.4 / max=0.996 with it.

* Apply the same backfill to RewardModelConfig.from_pretrained; Path-typed backfill

Review follow-up: RewardModelConfig.from_pretrained has the identical
pattern (parse + return, no backfill), and PreTrainedRewardModel /
make_reward_model call it directly — e.g. RobometerRewardModel.__init__
branches on config.pretrained_path is None, so a direct from_pretrained
call took the 'fresh model' branch instead of loading the checkpoint.

Also assigns Path(model_id) on the policy side to match the Path | None
field type, and adds the hub-id + pinned-revision test case (hf_hub_download
mocked) alongside the RewardModelConfig regression test.

* style: satisfy ruff format in test_pretrained_path_backfill

---------

ns0:entry.ns0:title: fix(envs): use VLABench instruction as description (#5022)
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
fix(envs): use VLABench instruction as description (#5022)

* fix(envs): use VLABench instruction as description

VLABenchEnv looked up `task_description` and `language_instruction`
on the VLABench task object. VLABench defines neither attribute; it
exposes the generated instruction through `task.get_instruction()`,
which its own evaluator and trajectory scripts call. Both hasattr()
checks therefore always failed and the env silently fell back to the
task name, so policies were prompted with "select_fruit" instead of
an instruction such as "Put the pear into the plate_seen".

This also diverged from training: the VLABench LeRobot datasets store
the full get_instruction() sentence as each episode's task.

Raise ValueError when VLABench returns no instruction instead of
falling back to the task name, which would keep this failure mode and
still report a score. The listed tasks should not hit this: each one
VLABench registers writes a non-empty instruction when it is built.
This matches MetaWorld, where a task without a description fails
with KeyError.

* fix(envs): clear rejected VLABench env

_ensure_env() stored the new env in self._env before checking its
task instruction, so raising on a missing instruction left the
rejected env in place. A caller that caught the ValueError and called
reset() again hit the early return in _ensure_env(), skipped the
check, and evaluated with an empty task_description. The rejected env
was also never closed.

Close and clear it before raising, using the same best-effort cleanup
that step() applies after a PhysicsError, so a retry rebuilds and
re-validates the env.

Co-authored-by: Jonathan D Faeth <210794222+JonnyFaeth@users.noreply.github.com>

ns0:entry.ns0:title: docs(robocasa): fix camera rename_map for smolvla_robocasa (#4860)
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
docs(robocasa): fix camera rename_map for smolvla_robocasa (#4860)

The RoboCasa365 eval snippets and the RoboCasa CI command mapped
`robot0_eye_in_hand` to `camera2` and `robot0_agentview_right` to
`camera3`, swapping the wrist and right agent views relative to how
`lerobot/smolvla_robocasa` was trained.

The checkpoint's own `train_config.json` and `policy_preprocessor.json`
both record `robot0_agentview_left` -> `camera1`,
`robot0_agentview_right` -> `camera2`, `robot0_eye_in_hand` -> `camera3`.
Since `--rename_map` replaces the checkpoint preprocessor's rename step
and all three views are 3x256x256, the mismatch was silently accepted.

ns0:entry.ns0:title: feat(optim): add opt-in fused Adam/AdamW flag (#5023)
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
feat(optim): add opt-in fused Adam/AdamW flag (#5023)

Fused Adam/AdamW kernels can shorten the optimizer step of large
policies, but there was no way to request them: policy presets
replace --optimizer.* and AdamWConfig had no fused field.

Add fused to AdamConfig and AdamWConfig and expose it as
optimizer_fused on act, groot, pi0, pi0.5, pi0_fast and smolvla.
The default stays None so PyTorch keeps choosing its implementation
(foreach on CUDA); a False default would force the slower for-loop
path instead.

A resumed run rebuilds its optimizer from the checkpoint's config, so
optimizer_fused has no effect there, as the docs now say. Overriding
--optimizer.fused between None and a bool on resume fails the
optimizer state load.

Co-authored-by: Pepijn <138571049+pkooij@users.noreply.github.com>

ns0:entry.ns0:title: fix(datasets): honour quantile_list in get_feature_stats (#4796)
ns0:entry.ns0:content:
fix(datasets): honour quantile_list in get_feature_stats (#4796)

get_feature_stats accepted a quantile_list but only used it for inputs
with fewer than two samples. For every other input it built
RunningQuantileStats() with the default quantiles, so a custom list was
silently replaced by q01/q10/q50/q90/q99. Pass the list through to the
running accumulator.
